ratings_why.fun: Choosing count, lump or churn is a real draft decision, but most payoffs end in plain +1/+1 buffs, and following two counters with many thresholds is work.
ratings_why.distinct: Debt as a fight resource that kills pay off, with the bill timed by Mr Magpie's slot, is unlike any of today's tribes, and the loan-shark fantasy is in the rules, not only the names.

verdict_why: The core reads well, but Mr Magpie, Uncle Jack and Thought and Memory have wording a player can't resolve at a glance.

points.text: In Mr Magpie, "Each Start of Turn it isn't" has no clear 'it'. Say "Each Start of Turn your Debt isn't repaid, gain 1 gold."

Repay payoffs are worded three ways ("when you repay", "whenever you repay", "repay 2 or more at once"), so Thought and Memory's "trigger twice" is unclear. Does it count twice against Grandchick's twice-a-turn limit, and does Wedding Magpie double? Say which.
On Uncle Jack, when the sale is worth more than your Debt, the text doesn't say whether the rest is paid in gold or lost. Say which.
Give repay payoffs one trigger word, such as "Repaid:", the way "When played:" works, so a glance at the board shows which units grow on repayment.
The seed's shiny-greed theme (stolen goods, evidence) is missing: everything is credit. A Skimmer that takes a small shiny item from the unit it kills would bring it in.

standouts.why: You move a magpie to the back row to put off the bill, then call it in. It's the theme as a board move, and you can see it.
The pawnbroker turns sales into repayments: one sentence, a real trade-off, and pure fantasy.
"Owe more, hit harder" reads instantly and makes borrowing in a fight feel like a gamble.

weakest.why: Rook borrows every turn and does nothing else, so on its own it reads as a trap.
Grandmother Corbie is the Long Ledger's matriarch, but her card is a quiet +1/+1 for each 10 in the Ledger with no grudge or memory in it.
Wassail Lender's "add 2 to your Debt" with no gold sits too close to Borrow and will be misread as Borrow.

flags.note: The 'it' in the gold clause is ambiguous.
How the doubling works with limited and threshold repay triggers isn't stated.
What happens to sale value above your Debt isn't stated.
With Silas Glint, The Belfry Mob's Skims may make Borrow free gold every fight, as the designer notes.
Arne with Thought and Memory on a Mr Magpie bill is a very large one-turn spike.
